title: OS Spec
description: The normalised intake and specification of one candidate OS, produced by phase 0 (Intake) and completed through phase 1 (Capability Definition). This is the object the whole build reads from. A field left out is a field the build will guess, and a guessed boundary is the most expensive defect OS Builder produces.

slug.description: Directory name under OS/ and the id used everywhere. Must not collide with an existing entry in OS/_registry.json.

capability.description: The repeatable professional capability in one sentence, explainable without the words folder, prompt or model.

primary_user.description: Who operates it, and what they already know. Decides how much the skill layer must teach.

problem.description: The observable failure today. Never stated as the absence of the solution.

desired_outcome.description: What is true afterwards that is not true now.

primary_artifact.description: The one thing it produces that a person keeps. An OS with no primary artifact is a chat persona.

workflow.description: The ordered operating steps. Three steps is the floor: fewer means a checklist, not a workflow.

non_scope.description: What it deliberately refuses to do. Never empty: an OS with no non scope absorbs every adjacent request until its boundary means nothing.

security_level.description: The MAXIMUM sensitivity class this OS will handle, not the typical one.

environment.description: Targets that must work. Anything absent here still needs a declared degradation in ADAPTERS/.

seam.description: Where this OS stops and that one starts.

constraints.description: Time, budget, tooling, jurisdiction, house rules.

modes.description: One row per operating mode. Becomes OS.md section 3.

human_approval_for.description: Actions the OS must never take without an explicit human decision. Never empty for an OS that can act on the world.

stop_conditions.description: The situations in which the correct output is a refusal. Every OS must be capable of saying STOP.

decision.description: The verdict of the SHOULD THIS BE AN OS tree. Recorded even when it is BUILD, so a later reader knows the question was asked.
